title: Surveyor 3
tagline: The robot that checked the Moon was safe for astronauts.
kicker: A true story from the Moon · 1967
mystery: Would a spacecraft with people sink into the Moon's dust?
p1.launch: 17 April 1967. Surveyor 3 heads for the Moon.
p1.hello: I'm Surveyor 3. I have something new: an arm that can dig!
p1.oops: Shiny rocks confused my radar, and my engine kept firing. Boing, boing!
p1.where: 20 April 1967, third touchdown: Oceanus Procellarum, the Ocean of Storms.
p2.camera: My camera looks into a mirror that turns to see all around me.
p2.hint: Tap a target, then hold until the picture is sent.
p2.s.horizon: Click! A grey plain all the way to the horizon.
p2.s.rocks: Click! Rocks and craters, big and small.
p2.s.foot: Click! Each picture took about 20 seconds to send.
p2.win: In less than an hour I began sending pictures. I sent 6,326 in all!
p3.question: People wanted to land here. Would the ground hold them up?
p3.hint: Tap a target, then hold to dig and to press.
p3.s.trench: I dug four trenches, all on commands from Earth.
p3.s.press: Press, and bump! Four bearing tests and thirteen impact tests.
p3.win: The soil is like wet sand: strong enough to hold up an Apollo Lunar Module!
p3.why: So astronauts could land safely on ground like this.
p4.night: Then the long, cold lunar night began.
p4.last: 4 May 1967: my last contact with Earth, two days into the night.
p5.visit: More than two years later, Apollo 12's Intrepid landed about 180 m away.
p5.parts: They took my scoop and camera home, to see what the Moon had done to them.
p5.proud: I told them the ground was safe. Then they came and stood right next to me!
p6.bye: I still stand in the Ocean of Storms. Look up at the Moon and wave!
